newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LEE SCORES FOR NEWCASTLE BUT CHARLTON FIGHT BACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEE SCORES FOR NEWCASTLE BUT CHARLTON FIGHT BACK.

text.p: England midfielder Robert Lee scored against his former club Charlton but the first division side fought back to draw 1-1 with Newcastle in the third round of the F.A. Cup on Sunday.
Lee, who played over 300 times for the Londoners before signing for Kevin Keegan's side four years ago, put Newcastle ahead after 33 minutes with a fortuitous goal.

Lee Clark crossed from the right and Alan Shearer rose at the far post to head the ball to Lee, who fluffed his first attempt completely -- inadvertently wrong-footing his marker -- before poking the ball into the net from eight metres.
Minutes earlier, first division Charlton had had what appeared to be legitimate appeals for a penalty turned down.
Paul Sturgess centred from the left to England under-21 forward Shaun Newton, who bustled past John Beresford only to be clearly hauled back by his shirt as he geared up for a shot.
The referee waved play on and within five minutes Newcastle were in front.
The premier league side, six times winners of England's leading cup competition, looked to be heading for the fourth round until 12 minutes from time when Mark Kinsella scored a stunning equaliser.
Picking the ball up in midfield, he strode forward and cracked a right-foot shot into the right-hand side of Shaka Hislop's net from 25 metres.
"It would have been (a perfect homecoming) but Charlton played really well and deserved their draw," said Lee, who will miss the replay at St James' Park due to suspension.
